name: Federal Republic of Germany
info: The West German state formed in 1949 from the three western occupation zones, which absorbed the German Democratic Republic in 1990 and became Europe's largest economy and a leading member of the European Union.

facts.capital: Bonn (provisional capital, 1949–1990); Berlin (capital again under the Berlin/Bonn Act of 1994, the government's move completed in 1999)
facts.predecessor: The Allied occupation zones of Germany (1945–1949), after the surrender of Nazi Germany on 8 May 1945; the German Democratic Republic (1949–1990) joined it at reunification

t: The western sectors held by France, the United Kingdom and the United States were merged on 23 May 1949 into the Federal Republic, which chose Bonn as a provisional capital to stress that two German states were meant to be temporary.

Marshall Plan aid and the Wirtschaftswunder from the early 1950s, NATO membership in 1955 and a founding place in the European Economic Community set West Germany's course; the Saarland joined on 1 January 1957.

Reunification on 3 October 1990 brought the five re-established eastern states into the Federal Republic, which regained full sovereignty on 15 March 1991 and is now the world's third-largest exporter and importer.
dyk: Germany has the world's oldest universal health care system, dating from Bismarck's social legislation of the 1880s; the Federal Republic still insures its population by statute, and spent 12.27% of its GDP on health in 2024.
ev: On 23 May the three western occupation zones are merged into the Federal Republic of Germany; Konrad Adenauer is elected the first federal chancellor and Bonn becomes the provisional capital.
West Germany joins NATO; it is a founding member of the European Economic Community.
On 1 January the Saarland joins West Germany.
On 3 October after the Two Plus Four Treaty, the German Democratic Republic is dissolved and its five re-established states accede to the Federal Republic.
On 15 March Germany regains its full sovereignty from the Allies.
Germany introduces the euro; the European Central Bank sits in Frankfurt.
Angela Merkel becomes the first female chancellor.
After Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Chancellor Olaf Scholz announces a one-time 100 billion euro infusion into the Bundeswehr and spending beyond NATO's 2% target.

sections.foundation:
The Federal Republic was built on the ruins of Nazi Germany. After the surrender of 8 May 1945 the Allies abolished the German state in law and divided Berlin and the remaining territory into four occupation zones; around 12 million ethnic Germans had been expelled from across Eastern Europe, and Germany had lost roughly a quarter of its pre-war territory. Surviving Nazi officials were tried at the Nuremberg trials. On 23 May 1949 the western sectors, controlled by France, the United Kingdom and the United States, were merged into the Federal Republic of Germany; on 7 October 1949 the Soviet Zone became the German Democratic Republic. The new state chose Bonn as a provisional capital to emphasise that the two-state solution was temporary.

West Germany was established as a federal parliamentary republic with a social market economy under the Grundgesetz, the Basic Law of 1949. Konrad Adenauer was elected the first federal chancellor that year. The country had already become a major recipient of Marshall Plan aid in 1948, and prolonged growth, the Wirtschaftswunder, began in the early 1950s. Its land ran from the North Sea and the Baltic to the Alps, divided into Länder with their own constitutions. Today the republic covers 357,022 square kilometres and has 84.7 million people by the 2023 census, the most populous member state of the European Union; Berlin is the largest city and the Ruhr the largest urban area.
sections.socioeconomy:
The social market economy of 1949 produced the Wirtschaftswunder and, after reunification, the largest economy in Europe by nominal GDP and the world's third-largest, sixth by purchasing power. Services make up about 72% of GDP, industry 27% (the largest manufacturing output in Europe) and agriculture 1%. Germany is the world's third-largest exporter and importer, with the second-largest trade surplus after China; its main exports are vehicles, machinery and chemicals. The automotive industry, with Volkswagen Group the world's second-largest producer, is the most competitive of its sectors; 29 of the Fortune Global 500 firms of 2024 were German, and the Mittelstand of specialised small and medium firms holds around 48% of the world's hidden champions.

Germany introduced the euro in 2002 and accounted for 28% of the eurozone economy in 2017. Research is a pillar of the economy, with the Max Planck Society, the Helmholtz Association and the Fraunhofer Society, and the dual apprenticeship system is copied around the world. The energy transition, the Energiewende, phased out the last nuclear plants in 2023 and met 40% of power demand from renewables in 2018. Since the 1970s deaths have exceeded births; the population is the world's fourth oldest, with an average age of 47.8, and grows by immigration: 23.8 million people, 28.7%, had a migration background in 2022. Christians were 49.7% in the 2022 census and Muslims an estimated 5.3–5.6 million.
sections.military:
The Federal Republic's armed forces, the Bundeswehr, are organised into the Heer with the KSK special forces, the Marine, the Luftwaffe and the Cyber and Information Domain Service. The constitution describes their role as defensive only, but a ruling of the Federal Constitutional Court in 1994 widened defence to crisis reaction and conflict prevention anywhere in the world. In peacetime the Minister of Defence commands; in a state of defence the Chancellor would become commander-in-chief. Military service was compulsory for men at eighteen until 2011, when it was suspended for a voluntary service, and women have served in all functions since 2001. In May 2024 the Bundeswehr had 180,215 active soldiers and 80,761 civilians.

West Germany joined NATO in 1955, faced the Berlin Wall from 1961 and eased tensions with the East through Willy Brandt's Ostpolitik in the late 1960s. After reunification Germany sent peacekeepers to the Balkans and troops to Afghanistan with NATO. Spending stayed below the alliance's 2% target, at $73.1 billion or 1.64% of GDP in 2023, until Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, when Chancellor Olaf Scholz announced a one-time infusion of 100 billion euros, almost double the 53 billion euro budget of 2021; in 2026 Germany reported $147 billion to NATO, 2.69% of GDP, and its spending in 2025 was the world's fourth-highest in absolute terms. About 3,000 troops serve abroad, 1,800 of them in Lithuania and its neighbours.
sections.governance:
Germany is a federal, parliamentary, representative democratic republic under the Basic Law of 1949. Legislative power rests with the Bundestag, elected by personalised proportional representation with a threshold of 5% or three seats, and the Bundesrat, whose members are appointed by the governments of the sixteen federated states. Amendments need two-thirds of both houses, and the principles of human dignity, the separation of powers, the federal structure and the rule of law are valid in perpetuity. The president, Frank-Walter Steinmeier since 2017, is head of state with mainly representative powers and is chosen by the Bundesversammlung of Bundestag members and state delegates; the chancellor, head of government, is appointed by the president after election by the party or coalition with most seats, Friedrich Merz since 2025.

Since 1949 the party system has been dominated by the centre-right Christian Democratic Union and the centre-left Social Democratic Party, which have supplied every chancellor, with the Free Democrats and Alliance 90/The Greens as junior partners; The Left has sat in the Bundestag since 2007 and the far-right Alternative for Germany since 2017. The civil law system rests on Roman law, with the Federal Constitutional Court holding judicial review, specialised supreme courts for labour, social, fiscal and administrative matters, and lay judges, the Schöffen, sitting with professionals on most criminal benches.
sections.impact:
The Federal Republic became the anchor of European integration. A founding member of the European Economic Community, it signed the Maastricht Treaty in 1992 and the Lisbon Treaty in 2007 and co-founded the eurozone; the European Central Bank sits in Frankfurt, its largest financial centre. Germany maintains 227 diplomatic missions and relations with more than 190 countries, belongs to the Council of Europe, NATO, the OECD, the G7, the G20, the World Bank and the IMF, has kept a strong alliance with France and all its neighbours since 1990 and is widely considered a great power. Its governments are close political allies of the United States, and it was the world's second-biggest aid donor in 2019.

Reunification made 3 October the national day, celebrated as German Unity Day since 1990. The country has the third-highest number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites, 55, and is a major destination for immigrants, second only to the United States; it took in over a million refugees and migrants during the 2015 crisis and recorded 1.06 million refugees from Ukraine by April 2023. German is the most widely spoken first language in the European Union. The Frankfurt Book Fair is the most important in the world for international deals, German films won the foreign-language Oscar in 1979, 2002 and 2007, the Berlinale has run since 1951, Kraftwerk and Tangerine Dream pioneered electronic music, and the national football team won the World Cup in 1954, 1974, 1990 and 2014.
sections.decline:
Reunification set the republic's tasks for a generation. United Germany was treated as the enlarged continuation of West Germany and kept its memberships; by the Berlin/Bonn Act of 1994 Berlin became the capital again while Bonn kept some ministries as a federal city, and the move of the government was completed in 1999. Modernisation of the East German economy was scheduled to last until 2019. The government approved a 50 billion euro stimulus in 2009, and the main projects of the early twenty-first century have been European integration, the Energiewende, the debt brake for balanced budgets, pronatalist measures and Industry 4.0. In the 2005 elections Angela Merkel became the first female chancellor.

The present decade has brought new strains. The far-right Alternative for Germany has sat in the Bundestag since 2017, and the fertility rate of 1.36 is far below replacement. Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 brought over a million refugees and a rearmament that carried defence spending past NATO's 2% target by 2026, with about 3,000 troops abroad. The last nuclear plants closed in 2023, when Germany was still the 14th-highest emitter of greenhouse gases, and violent crime reached a fifteen-year high in 2024. Church membership has fallen: a 2025 study estimated 48.1% of the population belonged to no religious organisation. Under Chancellor Friedrich Merz since 2025 the Federal Republic remains Europe's largest economy and a pillar of the European Union.

summary: The Federal Republic of Germany was formed on 23 May 1949 from the three western occupation zones, grew through the Wirtschaftswunder into a founding member of the EEC and NATO, absorbed the German Democratic Republic on 3 October 1990 and regained full sovereignty in 1991. Today it is Europe's largest economy, the world's third-largest exporter and a great power inside the European Union.
references: Mary Fulbrook, A Concise History of Germany (Cambridge University Press, 1991)
Tony Judt, Postwar: A History of Europe Since 1945 (Penguin, 2005)

pointDescs.1949: The three western zones are merged into the Federal Republic on 23 May; the Basic Law takes effect and Konrad Adenauer becomes the first chancellor.
pointDescs.1955: West Germany joins NATO and is a founding member of the European Economic Community; the Wirtschaftswunder is under way.
pointDescs.1957: The Saarland joins West Germany on 1 January.
pointDescs.1961: East Germany builds the Berlin Wall to stop its citizens escaping to the West; the Federal Republic prospers behind the Cold War frontier.
pointDescs.1990: Reunification on 3 October: the five re-established eastern states accede to the Federal Republic after the Two Plus Four Treaty.
pointDescs.1991: Germany regains its full sovereignty from the Allies on 15 March.
pointDescs.2002: The euro replaces the mark; Germany has signed Maastricht in 1992 and the government has completed its move to Berlin in 1999.
pointDescs.2005: Angela Merkel becomes the first female chancellor.
pointDescs.2009: The government approves a 50 billion euro stimulus plan in the financial crisis.
pointDescs.2015: Germany takes in over a million refugees and migrants; its economy, the largest in Europe, is at its height.
pointDescs.2022: Russia's invasion of Ukraine brings over a million Ukrainian refugees and a 100 billion euro rearmament.
pointDescs.2025: Friedrich Merz becomes chancellor; Germany is the world's third-largest economy and exporter and, in 2026, reports defence spending of 2.69% of GDP.

notes: The registered start 1949 is the Federal Republic itself; the Holy Roman Empire, the Empire of 1871, Weimar and Nazi Germany are kept to the foundation paragraph.
The article names no founder; Adenauer is given as the first chancellor. The capital fact lists Bonn and Berlin in order.
References are the two works in the article's Sources section; Murdoch concerns Roman Germania, not this state. Drop it if a work on the period alone is wanted.

The curve puts the peak at 2015 and 2025: the article gives no economic series, so the shape is a judgement from its ranking statements (largest economy in Europe, third-largest exporter, defence spending above 2% by 2026).
Cultural items in impact (Oscars, Berlinale, football) are from the article's culture and sports sections and are dated to the republic's years.
